question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, who can contribute to the corpus of a Category III AIF?

answer.text: Indian, foreign, and NRI investors — with minimum investment of INR 1 crore per investor (INR 25 lakh for employees/directors of AIF or Manager), corpus minimum INR 20 crore, and maximum 1000 investors per scheme.
Only individual HNIs with minimum investment of INR 50 lakh.
Only foreign portfolio investors with RBI approval.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Indian, foreign, and NRI investors can all contribute to an AIF corpus. The minimum investment per investor is INR 1 crore (INR 25 lakh for employees/directors of the AIF or Manager). Each scheme must have minimum corpus of INR 20 crore. Maximum investors per scheme = 1000. Capital is raised only through private placement. Accredited Investors (AI) enjoy flexibility on minimum investment amount (under the AI-only funds regime notified w.e.f. August 3, 2021). **The Trap:** Option B wrongly excludes foreign/NRI investors. Option C understates the INR 1 cr minimum. Option D wrongly narrows to FPIs. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C, XIX-D, XIX-A, XIX-B all test this foundational rule. Not swapped across categories — identical numbers for Cat I/II/III. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For a Cat III fund, foreign investor inflows come via FEMA route + FPI regulations + tax treaty considerations. NRI investors can invest on a repatriable or non-repatriable basis, which affects redemption currency. Employees/directors investing at the INR 25 lakh floor help boost skin-in-the-game optics but don't substitute for the 5%/10 cr sponsor commitment.
